issue_context.title: Display ranking details at search
issue_context.body:
Related product team resources: [roadmap card](https://www.notion.so/meilisearch/ef7d86c80ef44c549e2361c70a367723?v=d11906bcef8b4b77815f84b801931c00&p=f09afa99f5ff4c34b82b480aab0ae726&pm=s) (_internal only_)
Related product discussions:
- https://github.com/meilisearch/product/discussions/594
- https://github.com/meilisearch/product/discussions/602

Related spec: WIP

## Motivation

Algolia does it and is requested by the users to migrate to Meilisearch.

## Usage

The purpose of this feature is to return ranking details for each document to understand and tweak the score of the documents more easily.

⚠️ Refer to the final spec to know the details and the final decisions about the usage.

## TODO

<!---Feel free to adapt this list with more technical/product steps-->

- [x] Release a prototype
- [x] If prototype validated, merge changes into `main`
- [ ] Update the spec

## Impacted teams

@meilisearch/docs-team and @meilisearch/integration-team
comments:
Part of this feature will be released as an experimental feature in Meilisearch v1.3:

- Computing the detailed scores per ranking rule for each document, available via the `showRankingScoreDetails` search query parameter. The detailed scores are **an experimental feature** in Meilisearch v1.3
- Computing aggregate, normalized ranking score per document, available via the `showRankingScore` search query parameter. The aggregate scores **are stabilized** in Meilisearch v1.3.

See the associated [product discussion](https://github.com/meilisearch/product/discussions/674) for more information.

To note: https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/3885 adds fields to score details that were not there in rc0 but will be there for rc1:
exactness.matchingWords
exactness.maxMatchingWords 

The specification has been updated to reflect this as well.

review_comments: I was ready to write a comment to tell you to use `fields_ids_map` in case `searchable_fields_ids` was `None`, but you did it already :D That's a detail of the codebase that is too tricky IMO.
That would be great :) but not strictly needed to do it in this PR IMO
oops 😶
it happens 😅
nice!
thanks I needed the computation laid out, anyway 😓

I assume you tested the score details feature with a placeholder search as well, and that it only returns the `Sort` score details? Also worth checking it when multiple `field:asc/desc` ranking rules exist.

> I assume you tested the score details feature with a placeholder search as well

Yes, with placeholder search, only the ranking rules that are applied in the placeholder search have details, so basically only sort and geosort.

> Also worth checking it when multiple field:asc/desc ranking rules exist.

can't be sure if I already checked, can check again.
I am always struggling to understand the difference between rank and score. Could this be documented at more points-of-use and/or renamed so that the definition of both is obvious?

I hesitated for a long time to make it so the "highest" rank is 0, and the worst rank is "max rank", so that they're ordinals, like in a race. But then I kinda want to start them at 1 instead of 0 😬 

Would maybe `Grade` or `Mark` work better than `Rank` for you?

Today the main distinction between rank and score is that the score is normalized by dividing the rank by its max rank.

Wording is important, so I'm very open to make the necessary changes here, I'm just a bit unsure what these are :-)
great explanation overall, but the word `rank` is used in its own definition :/
would it make it better to use `grade` or `mark` in the fields (`the ordinal rank` is exactly what it is, IMO)?

hmm... I don't think this is technically correct. We could return documents whose value for this field is different than `null` (ie field doesn't exist, or contains an empty array, or maybe even an object). It doesn't necessarily make it wrong, but it is tricky.

the meaning of `score_details::Sort::value` is intended to be "the value that was used to sort this document, or `null` if no value was used to sort this document (because it has no value for this field, an object for this field, or an empty array for this field).

As a result I feel this is consistent with this definition?

Maybe it should be documented in the `score_details` module though?
The 2D point that was added to the `VecDeque` here will always be the same, right?

Not in my understanding.

- The first `u32` is the public id of the document
- The 2D point is the geopoint of that document.

I don't think it is expected that consecutive entries in this queue are all at the same point. The only rule is that they are stored in increasing (decreasing?) distance from the target point.
oops, sorry, you're completely right!
rename to `WordsRank`? `Words`, `Typo`, etc. are starting to be too overloaded

these are meant to be used prefixed by the module name, so I followed the convention of not repeating context that can be inferred from the module name.

Users should use the qualified `score_details::Words` form, or too verbose, `use score_details::Words as WordsScore`.

Should they still be qualified?
I get the argument for using simply `Words`, do whatever is best for you :)
I think I prefer keeping `Words` for now, I'll see if some other reviewers have the same comment :-)
